results.label: scam
results.text: USPS: Your package could not be delivered due to an unpaid customs fee of $1.99. Pay within 12 hours or it will be returned: http://usps-redelivery-help.top/pay
results.summary: This is a fake USPS text trying to steal $1.99 via a look-alike link that is not usps.com.

results.label: scam
results.text: FedEx: We attempted delivery but nobody was home. Confirm your address and reschedule here: fedex-reschedule-now.info/track?id=88213
results.summary: This is a fake FedEx delivery text. The link is not FedEx’s real website (fedex.com) and is designed to steal your address and payment details.

results.label: scam
results.text: DHL Express: your parcel is held at our depot. A customs charge of $2.45 is required. Pay at dhl-customs-pay.xyz to release it.
results.summary: This is a fake DHL delivery message sending you to a lookalike payment site that is not DHL's real website.

results.label: scam
results.text: NJ E-ZPass: You have an unpaid toll balance of $12.50. To avoid a $50 late fee, pay by today: ezpass-nj-tollpay.top/inv
results.summary: This is a fake toll-payment text impersonating NJ E-ZPass — the link uses an unofficial .top domain that does not resolve and pressures you to pay today to avoid a $50 fee.

results.label: scam
results.text: Chase Alert: Unusual $849.00 charge on your card. If this was not you, verify now or your account will be locked: chase-secure-verify.top/login
results.summary: This is not a real Chase message — the link goes to a fake domain that impersonates Chase to steal your login, and Chase’s official site is only chase.com.

results.label: scam
results.text: Wells Fargo: Your account has been temporarily restricted. Call our fraud department at 1-855-555-0113 immediately to restore access.
results.summary: This is a fake Wells Fargo alert trying to get you to call a scammer's number — Wells Fargo did not send it.

results.label: scam
results.text: Bank of America: we detected a login from a new device. To cancel, reply with the 6-digit code we just sent you.
results.summary: This message impersonates Bank of America to steal your login code — legitimate banks never ask you to reply with a one-time code.

results.label: scam
results.text: Zelle: A payment of $500 to you is pending because your account is not upgraded. Send $100 to unlock it, you will be refunded instantly.
results.summary: This is a Zelle advance-fee scam — a fake $500 pending payment is used to trick you into sending $100 with a false promise of an instant refund.

results.label: scam
results.text: Venmo: you were sent $350 by mistake. Please return it via this link right away or your account will be suspended: venmo-refund-help.click/r
results.summary: This is a fake Venmo message trying to get you to click a lookalike link to return money, threatening account suspension if you don't.

results.label: scam
results.text: PayPal invoice #INV-44821 for $479.99 (Norton antivirus renewal) has been paid. If you did not authorize this, call 1-888-555-0177 within 24 hours to cancel.
results.summary: This is a fake PayPal invoice callback scam - it pretends you were charged $479.99 and pressures you to call a fake support number to steal money or remote access.

results.label: scam
results.text: Amazon: Your order of an iPhone 15 Pro for $1,149 has been placed. If you did not make this purchase call 1-877-555-0166 to cancel.
results.summary: This is a fake Amazon order alert trying to get you to call a scammer's number to 'cancel' - check your real Amazon account instead.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, this is Mark from the Amazon billing team. Your account has a security hold. To clear it purchase two $500 Amazon gift cards and read me the codes.
results.summary: This is a gift-card scam impersonating Amazon billing — Amazon never asks you to buy gift cards to clear a security hold.

results.label: scam
results.text: IRS FINAL NOTICE: You owe $2,847 in back taxes. A warrant will be issued for your arrest today. Call 855-555-0142 immediately and pay with Apple gift cards. Do not tell anyone.
results.summary: This is a fake IRS arrest threat demanding gift card payment, which the real IRS never does.

results.label: scam
results.text: This is the Social Security Administration. Your social security number has been suspended due to suspicious activity. Call 855-555-0150 or a warrant will be issued for your arrest.
results.summary: This is a scam impersonating the Social Security Administration with a fake arrest threat to pressure you into calling.

results.label: scam
results.text: Medicare: you are eligible for a new 2026 benefits card with $1,200 in grocery allowance. Reply YES and confirm your Medicare number to receive it.
results.summary: This is a Medicare impersonation scam - Medicare does not text to offer a new $1,200 grocery benefits card or ask you to confirm your Medicare number by replying YES.

results.label: scam
results.text: Apple ID: Your iCloud account is locked due to suspicious activity. Verify within 24h or all photos will be deleted: apple-id-unlock.support/verify
results.summary: This is a fake Apple/iCloud lockout message designed to steal your Apple ID – the link is not on Apple's real domains and uses a lookalike address plus threats about deleting photos.

results.label: scam
results.text: WARNING: Your computer is infected with 5 viruses! Do not turn off your PC. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-800-555-0123.
results.summary: This is a fake tech-support pop-up impersonating Microsoft to scare you into calling a scammer phone number.

results.label: scam
results.text: Geek Squad: your 3-year protection plan renews today for $389.99. To cancel and get a refund call 1-866-555-0188.
results.summary: This is a fake Geek Squad renewal invoice trying to get you to call a scammer phone number for a “refund” — Geek Squad does not send unsolicited renewal charges like this.

results.label: scam
results.text: Netflix: your payment failed and your account will be closed. Update billing now: netflix-billing-update.top/account
results.summary: This is a fake Netflix payment alert — the link uses a lookalike domain that is not Netflix's official site and tries to pressure you to update billing.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi Sarah, are we still on for dinner Friday? Let me know!
results.summary: This is a classic wrong-number opener that greets you by name to start a conversation — harmless if from someone you know, but often used to lead into a scam later.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hello, I got your number from a friend. I'm Emily, I just moved to the city and don't know anyone. Can we chat? 😊
results.summary: This is an unsolicited friendly introduction from a stranger inviting you to chat, which is a common first step in wrong-number / relationship-building scams.

results.label: scam
results.text: I've been making $3,000 a week with a crypto trading platform my uncle taught me. I can show you how, small deposit of $250 to start, guaranteed returns. Message me on WhatsApp.
results.summary: This is an investment scam offering impossible guaranteed crypto profits of $3,000 a week from a $250 deposit and pushing you to WhatsApp to send money.

results.label: scam
results.text: My dear, I am a US Army engineer deployed overseas. I have fallen in love with you. I need $800 in iTunes cards to take leave and come meet you.
results.summary: This is a classic romance / military impersonation scam asking for $800 in iTunes gift cards so a supposed US Army engineer can take leave to meet you.

results.label: scam
results.text: Grandma it's me, I'm in jail and I need bail money, please don't tell mom and dad. Can you send $2,400 in Google Play cards? A lawyer will call you.
results.summary: This is a classic “grandparent in jail” scam asking for bail in gift cards and secrecy — real police, courts and lawyers never take Google Play cards.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi! We found your resume. Remote job, earn $200-$400 per day liking videos. No experience needed. Contact our manager on Telegram @workfromhome_jobs to start today.
results.summary: Unsolicited Telegram job offering $200-$400/day for liking videos after "finding your resume" is a classic task-scam that leads to advance fees or account theft.

results.label: scam
results.text: Congratulations on the personal assistant job! Enclosed is a check for $3,800. Deposit it and send $1,500 via Zelle to our equipment vendor, keep the rest as your pay.
results.summary: This is a classic fake-check scam: you are asked to deposit a check you received and send part of the money onward via Zelle, then the original check bounces and you lose what you sent.

results.label: scam
results.text: CONGRATULATIONS! You've won $750,000 in the Mega Millions International Lottery. To claim, send a $199 processing fee. Reply with your full name and bank details.
results.summary: This is an advance-fee lottery scam: you didn't enter to win, and real lotteries never require a processing fee or bank details by reply to claim a prize.

results.label: scam
results.text: Coinbase: a withdrawal of 0.8 BTC is pending. If this was not you, secure your wallet immediately by entering your 12-word recovery phrase: coinbase-secure-wallet.info
results.summary: This message impersonates Coinbase and tries to steal your wallet by asking for your 12-word recovery phrase on a fake non-Coinbase website.

results.label: scam
results.text: You are eligible for a tax refund of $1,462.18. Submit your request and bank details here to receive the payment: gov-taxrefund-claim.top
results.summary: This is a fake tax refund phishing message trying to steal your bank details via a non-official lookalike site, not the IRS.

results.label: scam

results.summary: This is a fake Duke Energy shut-off threat trying to make you pay with Bitcoin — real utilities never demand payment by Bitcoin ATM.

results.label: scam
results.text: Hi, are you at your desk? I need you to buy 5 Target gift cards for a client gift, $200 each. I'm in a meeting so can't talk. I'll reimburse you today. Send me the codes. - Jim, CEO
results.summary: This is a classic CEO impersonation scam asking you to buy gift cards and send the codes — legitimate bosses never request this by email or text.

results.label: scam
